podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins performed drums on records by Ozzy Osborne. This collaboration highlights his versatility and the respect he garnered within the rock community. "He also showed up in records by Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John."

podcast.title: Tribute After Death
podcast.body: Ozzy Osborne was among the many musicians who sent tributes upon Taylor Hawkins' death, underscoring the widespread respect and admiration he commanded from his peers. "When he died, tributes came in from everyone from Ozzy Osborne to Stevie Nicks, to Travis Barker, to Tom Morello to Liam Gallagher."

xref.title: Plane Crash Death (1982)
xref.body: On March 19, 1982, Randy Rhoads, who was Ozzy Osbourne's guitarist, died in a plane crash. The Beech Bonanza he was in crashed into a house after the pilot clipped a wing while "buzzing" Ozzy's tour bus, leading to the fatal accident. "Randy Rhodes, Ozzy Osborne's guitarist, died when the beach bananzen he was in, crashed into a house after the pilot clipped a wing, buzzing Ozzy's tour bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ozzfest Tour (2000)
xref.body: By the summer of 2000, P.O.D., a band composed of born-again Christians, embarked on a tour with Ozzy Osbourne, known as the "Prince of Darkness," as part of Ozzfest. This unusual pairing was humorously characterized as "sabotaging Satan's music from the inside." "By the summer of 2000s this band of born again was on the road with the Prince of Darkness, Ozzy Osborne and that year's version of Osfest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Rock Tattoo Adopter
xref.body: Ozzy Osbourne is identified as one of the first rock stars noticed with visible tattoos by many, including Darren Fyfer. He had tattoos early on, particularly on his hands, arms, and shoulders, which contributed to the perception of him being "in a rock and roll." "Ozzy Osborne, for sure. He had a few tattoos early on. And I remember thinking, well, that's cool. He must, he's in a rock and roll. He's in a rock and roll. That idea of a tattoo, that much cooler."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guest Appearances and Collaborations
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was known for his willingness to assist other bands and artists. He performed on albums by Coheed and Cambria (also touring with them), Eric Avery (Jane's Addiction bassist), Chris Shiflett (Foo Fighter, for Jackson United project), Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John. "And like his boss and friend, Taylor was always willing to help out other bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: Following the breakup, members pursued various endeavors: other bands like Imperial Teen and Mr. Bungle were formed, some made guest appearances and received production credits, and record labels were established. Drummer Mike Bordin worked with Ozzy Osborne for a period, and guitarist Jim Martin transitioned to growing 1,300-pound pumpkins professionally. "Drummer Mike Bowden went off to work with Ozzy Osborne for a while."

xref.title: Near-Fatal Manicure Infection
xref.body: In 2018, Ozzy Osbourne contracted a severe, near-fatal infection following a manicure. His thumb became so infected that it swelled to the size of a light bulb, requiring hospitalization and aggressive antibiotic treatment to prevent the loss of his hand. "Ozzy Osborne contracted a near-fatal infection in 2018. After a manicure, his thumb became so infected that it reached the sides of a light bulb."

xref.title: Video Evidence of Early Headbanging
xref.body: Video evidence from a Black Sabbath gig in Paris in 1970 shows both Ozzy Osborne and Geezer Butler engaging in headbanging, providing early documentation of the practice within modern rock music. "Moving deeper into 1970, there's video evidence of both Ozzy Osborne and Geeser Butler head banging during a black Sabbath gig in Paris."
